title: He lā maʻamau
description: Ten short stories about everyday life in Hawaiʻi: school mornings, work, films, illness, study, hula, trips, history and the neighbourhood.

lessons.title: Ka makuakāne ʻo Kanoa
lessons.summary: On an ordinary school day Kanoa takes his two children to school, although his son would rather stay home and play.
lessons.text:
He makuakāne ʻo Kanoa. Noho ʻo ia me kona ʻohana ma Kapolei. He ʻelua keiki a Kanoa: ʻo Akoni lāua ʻo Kēhau. He ʻohana maikaʻi kēia.

Ma ka lā maʻamau, lawe ʻo Kanoa i kāna mau keiki i ke kula. Ma hope, hele ʻo ia i kāna hana. He lā maʻamau kēia no ka ʻohana.

I kēia lā, ʻaʻole ʻo Akoni makemake e hele i ke kula. Makemake ʻo ia e pāʻani ma ka hale. "He lā kula kēia," wahi a ka makuakāne. "Hele nā keiki a pau i ke kula." Makemake nō ʻo Kēhau e hele.

Ua lawe ʻo Kanoa i nā keiki ʻelua i ke kula. Ma ke kula, ua pāʻani ʻo Akoni me nā keiki ʻē aʻe, a ua aʻo ʻo ia i kekahi mele hou.

Ma hope o ke kula, ua pau kā Kanoa hana. Ua hele mai ʻo ia e lawe i nā keiki i ka hale. "He lā maikaʻi nō kēia!" wahi a Akoni.

Nā nīnau:
Noho ʻo Kanoa me kona ʻohana ma Kailua?
ʻAʻole, noho ʻo ia me kona ʻohana ma Kapolei.
Makemake ʻo Akoni e hele i ke kula i kēia lā?
ʻAʻole, makemake ʻo ia e pāʻani ma ka hale.
Na wai i lawe i kā Kanoa mau keiki i ke kula?
Na ko lāua makuakāne, ʻo Kanoa.
He lā maikaʻi kēia no Akoni?
He lā maikaʻi nō ia no Akoni.

lessons.title: Ma ka waihona kālā
lessons.summary: Healani counts money and serves people at a bank in Honolulu, from an old man who comes often to a child with a single dollar.
lessons.text:
Hana ʻo Healani ma kekahi waihona kālā ma Honolulu. I kēlā me kēia lā, hele ʻo ia i laila ma mua o nā kānaka ʻē aʻe. Komo ʻo ia i loko o ka waihona, a helu ʻo ia i ke kālā. ʻAʻole he miliona kālā ma laila, akā he nui nō.

Ma hope, komo mai nā kānaka, a lawelawe ʻo Healani iā lākou. Komo mai kekahi kāne kahiko. Hele pinepine mai kēia kāne i ka waihona. Makemake ʻo ia i kekahi kālā. Helu ʻo Healani i ke kālā, a lawe ke kāne i kāna kālā.

Ma hope, komo mai kekahi wahine me kāna keiki. Hoʻokahi wale nō kālā a ke keiki. Makemake ʻo ia e mālama i kāna kālā ma ka waihona. Ua lawelawe ʻo Healani i ke keiki e like me kēlā kāne kahiko. "I kēia lā, hoʻokahi kālā; ma hope, he miliona!" wahi a ka wahine.

Ma hope, pau ka hana. Helu hou ʻo Healani i ke kālā a pau, a hoʻi ʻo ia i ka hale. He lā maʻamau kēia no Healani.

Nā nīnau:
Hana ʻo Healani ma hea?
Hana ʻo ia ma kekahi waihona kālā ma Honolulu.
He miliona kālā ma ka waihona?
ʻAʻole he miliona kālā ma laila, akā he nui nō.
Hele pinepine mai ke kāne kahiko i ka waihona?
Hele pinepine mai nō ʻo ia i laila.
He nui ke kālā a ke keiki?
ʻAʻole, hoʻokahi wale nō kālā a ke keiki.

lessons.title: Ke kiʻiʻoniʻoni hou
lessons.summary: Three children find nothing good on TV, look up a new film on the internet and go to see it with their mother.
lessons.text:
He ʻekolu keiki a Kalena: ʻo Kaipo, ʻo Kawehi a me Nāinoa. I kekahi lā, makemake nā keiki ʻekolu e nānā i ke kīwī. Nānā lākou i ke kīwī, akā ʻaʻole maikaʻi nā polokalamu. He mau polokalamu kahiko wale nō.

ʻImi ʻo Kaipo i kekahi mea ma ka pūnaewele. Loaʻa iā ia kekahi wikiō no kekahi kiʻiʻoniʻoni hou. Nānā nā keiki ʻekolu i ka wikiō. He kiʻiʻoniʻoni ia no kekahi wahine kaulana o ka wā kahiko. "Maikaʻi paha kēia kiʻiʻoniʻoni," wahi a Kawehi.

Nānā pū ʻo Kalena i ka wikiō. Manaʻo ʻo ia, he kiʻiʻoniʻoni maikaʻi paha ia. ʻImi ʻo ia i ka manawa o ke kiʻiʻoniʻoni ma ka pūnaewele. Ua hele lākou a pau i ka hale kiʻiʻoniʻoni ma Kapolei, a ua nānā lākou i ke kiʻiʻoniʻoni hou. Maikaʻi loa ka hopena: ma ka hopena, ua hoʻi ka wahine i kona ʻāina.

Ma hope, ua hoʻi lākou i ka hale. "Maikaʻi ke kīwī a me ka pūnaewele," wahi a Nāinoa, "akā maikaʻi loa ke kiʻiʻoniʻoni!"

Nā nīnau:
He ʻekolu keiki a Kalena?
He ʻekolu nō keiki a Kalena: ʻo Kaipo, ʻo Kawehi a me Nāinoa.
Maikaʻi nā polokalamu o ke kīwī?
ʻAʻole, he mau polokalamu kahiko wale nō.
Ma hea i ʻimi ai ʻo Kaipo?
Ua ʻimi ʻo ia ma ka pūnaewele.
Ma ka hopena o ke kiʻiʻoniʻoni, ua hoʻi ka wahine i hea?
Ua hoʻi ʻo ia i kona ʻāina.

lessons.title: Ua maʻi ʻo Kamaka
lessons.summary: Little Kamaka is sick, so his father stays home with him and his mother brings him a present.
lessons.text:
Ua maʻi ʻo Kamaka. He keiki liʻiliʻi ʻo ia. Ma muli o kona maʻi, ʻaʻole ʻo ia i hele i ke kula i kēia lā. Pono ʻo ia e noho ma ka hale.

He pilikia kēia no kona makuakāne, ʻo Iokepa, no ka mea he nui kāna hana i kēia lā. Akā ʻoiai he nui kāna hana, noho ʻo Iokepa me Kamaka. "Pono ka makuakāne e noho me ke keiki maʻi," wahi a Iokepa. Kākoʻo nā kānaka o kāna ʻoihana iā ia, a kākoʻo pū kāna wahine, ʻo Mahealani. ʻAʻole he pilikia nui.

Hāʻawi ʻo Iokepa i kekahi puke kiʻi liʻiliʻi iā Kamaka.

Ma hope, hoʻi mai ʻo Mahealani me kekahi makana no Kamaka: he puke mele hou. "Aloha, e Kamaka," wahi a Mahealani, a hāʻawi ʻo ia i ka makana iā ia. Nui ke aloha o Kamaka no kona makuakāne a me Mahealani.

Ma hope o ʻelua lā, ua ola hou ʻo Kamaka, a ua hoʻi ʻo ia i ke kula me kāna makana.

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha ʻaʻole ʻo Kamaka i hele i ke kula?
Ma muli o kona maʻi, ʻaʻole ʻo ia i hele i ke kula.
Ua noho ʻo Iokepa ma ka hale me Kamaka?
Ua noho nō ʻo ia ma ka hale, ʻoiai he nui kāna hana.
He aha ka makana a Mahealani?
He puke mele hou ka makana.
Ua ola hou ʻo Kamaka?
Ua ola hou nō ʻo ia ma hope o ʻelua lā.

lessons.title: Ka noiʻi a Kanani
lessons.summary: Kanani studies ocean science at the university in Mānoa and writes up her research before she graduates.
lessons.text:
Hele ʻo Kanani i ke kulanui ma Mānoa. Aʻo ʻo ia i ka ʻepekema o ke kai. He kulanui nui ia, a he nui nā kānaka e aʻo ana i ka ʻepekema ma laila.

I kēia makahiki, he papahana noiʻi kā Kanani. Noiʻi ʻo ia i ke kai ma Kāneʻohe. Ke hoʻololi ʻia nei ke kai e nā kānaka, a he mea koʻikoʻi kēia no nā kānaka a pau o ka honua. He papahana koʻikoʻi kāna.

Hoʻohana ʻo Kanani i kekahi ʻenehana hou. Ua hoʻomohala ʻia kēia ʻenehana ma ke kulanui. Me ka ʻenehana, ʻike ʻo ia i ke kai i nā lā a pau.

Ma hope, kākau ʻo Kanani i kāna noiʻi. He 40 ʻaoʻao kāna moʻolelo noiʻi. Kōkua kona kumu iā ia me kēlā me kēia ʻaoʻao.

I kēia makahiki, e puka ana ʻo Kanani mai ke kulanui. Ma hope o kona puka ʻana, makemake ʻo ia e hoʻomohala i nā ʻenehana hou, a e hoʻololi i ka manaʻo o nā kānaka no ke kai.

Nā nīnau:
Aʻo ʻo Kanani i ka ʻepekema o ke kai?
Aʻo nō ʻo ia i ka ʻepekema o ke kai ma ke kulanui ma Mānoa.
He papahana koʻikoʻi kā Kanani?
He papahana koʻikoʻi nō ia, no ka mea ke hoʻololi ʻia nei ke kai.
He 40 ʻaoʻao kāna moʻolelo noiʻi?
He 40 ʻaoʻao nō kāna moʻolelo noiʻi.
E puka ana ʻo Kanani i kēia makahiki?
E puka ana nō ʻo ia mai ke kulanui i kēia makahiki.

lessons.title: Ka hoʻokūkū hula
lessons.summary: A hula class in Kahului learns a new dance for the October contest, and it wins.
lessons.text:
I ʻOkakopa o kēlā me kēia makahiki, he hoʻokūkū hula ma Kahului, ma Maui. Hula ʻo Pualani me kekahi papa hula. Makemake ka papa e lanakila i ka hoʻokūkū o kēia makahiki.

ʻO Kauʻi ke kumu hula. Ua hoʻolālā ʻo ia i ka hula no ka hoʻokūkū. Ua haku ʻo ia i kekahi mele hou. He mele ia no ka ʻāina a me ka moʻomeheu o Maui. "He mea koʻikoʻi ka moʻomeheu Hawaiʻi," wahi a Kauʻi.

Ua hoʻolālā pū ʻo Kauʻi i ka neʻe ʻana o nā wāhine ma ke kahua. Aʻo nā wāhine i ka hula i nā lā a pau, a hiki i ʻOkakopa.

I ka lā o ka hoʻokūkū, neʻe ka papa i ke kahua. Hoʻokani ʻo Kauʻi i ka pahu, a hula nā wāhine i ka mele hou. Ma ka hopena, ua lanakila ka papa o Pualani! "He lanakila kēia no ka moʻomeheu o Maui," wahi a Kauʻi.

Nā nīnau:
Aia ka hoʻokūkū hula ma Kahului?
Aia nō ka hoʻokūkū hula ma Kahului, i ʻOkakopa.
Na wai i haku i ka mele hou?
Na Kauʻi, ke kumu hula, i haku i ka mele hou.
Ua hoʻokani ʻo Kauʻi i ka pahu?
Ua hoʻokani nō ʻo ia i ka pahu ma ka hoʻokūkū.
Ua lanakila ka papa o Pualani?
Ua lanakila nō ka papa o Pualani.

lessons.title: He huakaʻi ma Oʻahu
lessons.summary: In July Makoa and his son Kainalu drive north to Haleʻiwa and west to Waiʻanae, then back south to Honolulu.
lessons.text:
I Iulai, ua hele ʻo Makoa me kāna keiki, ʻo Kainalu, ma kekahi huakaʻi ma Oʻahu. Na Makoa i hoʻokele.

Mai Honolulu, ua hoʻokele lāua i ka ʻākau, i Haleʻiwa. Ma laila, ua nānā lāua i ke kai ma ka ʻaoʻao ʻākau o ka mokupuni.

Ma hope, ua hoʻokele lāua i ke komohana, i Waiʻanae. He ʻāpana kahiko ʻo Waiʻanae, a noho nā kānaka maoli ma laila mai ka wā kahiko mai. Ua hele lāua i luna o kekahi wahi kiʻekiʻe. He nui nā pōhaku ʻoi ma laila, a ua hele lāua me ka mālama ma luna o nā pōhaku ʻoi. Mai luna aku, ua nānā lāua i ke kai ma lalo. "He maikaʻi maoli!" wahi a Kainalu.

Ma hope, ua hoʻi lāua ma ka hema, i Honolulu. Aia ko lāua hale ma ka ʻaoʻao hema o ka mokupuni. Ua ʻike lāua i ʻelua ʻāpana o Oʻahu i ka lā hoʻokahi. "He huakaʻi maikaʻi maoli kēia," wahi a Makoa.

Nā nīnau:
Ua hele ʻo Makoa lāua ʻo Kainalu ma kekahi huakaʻi i Iulai?
Ua hele nō lāua ma kekahi huakaʻi i Iulai.
Ua hele lāua i Haleʻiwa, ma ka ʻākau?
Ua hele nō lāua i Haleʻiwa, ma ka ʻākau.
Aia ʻo Waiʻanae ma ke komohana o Oʻahu?
Aia nō ʻo Waiʻanae ma ke komohana o Oʻahu.
Ua nānā lāua i ke kai mai kahi kiʻekiʻe?
Ua nānā nō lāua i ke kai ma lalo, mai kahi kiʻekiʻe aku.

lessons.title: Ma ka hōʻikeʻike
lessons.summary: Nāone's class visits an exhibition in Honolulu about the chiefs and kings of the Hawaiian kingdom.
lessons.text:
Ua hele ka papa o Nāone i kekahi hōʻikeʻike ma Honolulu. He hōʻikeʻike ia no nā aliʻi a me nā mōʻī o ka wā kahiko.

Ma ka hōʻikeʻike, ua ʻike nā keiki i nā kiʻi o nā aliʻi. Ua aʻo lākou no Kamehameha, ka mōʻī mua o nā mokupuni a pau. He nui nā kaua i kēlā wā. Ua kaua ʻo Kamehameha me nā aliʻi ʻē aʻe, a ua lanakila ʻo ia. Nui loa kona mana. Ua make ʻo ia i ka makahiki 1819.

Ma hope, ua lilo ʻo Kalākaua i mōʻī. Ua kūkulu ʻo ia i ka hale aliʻi ʻo ʻIolani ma Honolulu. Ua kūkulu ʻia ka hale i ka makahiki 1882.

I kēlā wā, he aupuni kūʻokoʻa ʻo Hawaiʻi. Ma hope o ka make ʻana o Kalākaua, ua lilo ʻo Liliʻuokalani i mōʻī wahine. I ka makahiki 1893, ua pau ke aupuni kūʻokoʻa. I kēia manawa, he mokuʻāina ʻo Hawaiʻi o ʻAmelika.

"He hōʻikeʻike maikaʻi loa kēia," wahi a Nāone. Ua aʻo nui ʻo ia no ka mana o nā aliʻi.

Nā nīnau:
ʻO wai ka mōʻī mua o nā mokupuni a pau?
ʻO Kamehameha ka mōʻī mua.
Ua make ʻo Kamehameha i ka makahiki 1819?
Ua make nō ʻo ia i ka makahiki 1819.
Na wai i kūkulu i ka hale aliʻi ʻo ʻIolani?
Na Kalākaua i kūkulu i ka hale aliʻi.
He mokuʻāina ʻo Hawaiʻi i kēia manawa?
He mokuʻāina nō ʻo Hawaiʻi o ʻAmelika i kēia manawa.

lessons.title: Ke kahua pāʻani o ke kaiāulu
lessons.summary: Leina, president of the Kalihi community group, gets the neighbours together to fix the small old playground where the children kept fighting.
lessons.text:
Aia kekahi kahua pāʻani kahiko ma ke kaiāulu o Kalihi. He kahua liʻiliʻi ia, a he kahiko nā mea pāʻani. Hakakā pinepine nā keiki ma laila, no ka mea liʻiliʻi loa ke kahua.

ʻO Leina ka pelekikena o ka hui o ke kaiāulu. Makemake ʻo ia e hoʻoponopono i ke kahua pāʻani. Ua hoʻolaha ʻo ia ma ka pūnaewele: he lā hana ma ke kahua pāʻani.

Hele mai ka poʻe o ke kaiāulu. ʻAʻole waiwai ka poʻe o Kalihi, akā he nui ko lākou aloha no nā keiki. Hoʻonohonoho ʻo Leina i nā kānaka. Māhele ʻo ia i ka hana: hoʻoponopono kekahi poʻe i nā mea pāʻani kahiko, a kūkulu kekahi poʻe i nā mea pāʻani hou. He māhele hana ko kēlā me kēia kanaka. Hoʻonohonoho pū ʻo ia i nā keiki e kōkua.

Ma ka hopena o ka lā, ua pau ka hana. ʻAʻole hakakā hou nā keiki. "ʻAʻole waiwai kēia kaiāulu i ke kālā, akā waiwai i ke aloha," wahi a ka pelekikena.

Nā nīnau:
ʻO wai ka pelekikena o ka hui o ke kaiāulu?
ʻO Leina ka pelekikena.
Ua hoʻolaha ʻo Leina ma ka pūnaewele?
Ua hoʻolaha nō ʻo ia ma ka pūnaewele.
Ua hakakā pinepine nā keiki ma ke kahua kahiko?
Ua hakakā pinepine nō lākou, no ka mea liʻiliʻi loa ke kahua.
Waiwai ka poʻe o Kalihi?
ʻAʻole waiwai lākou i ke kālā, akā waiwai lākou i ke aloha.

lessons.title: Ka puke a Kamalei
lessons.summary: Kamalei writes a Hawaiian children's book; it is printed and released in January and reaches first place among books in Hawaiʻi.
lessons.text:
He kumu ʻo Kamalei ma kekahi kula ma Wailuku. Ua kākau ʻo ia i kekahi puke no nā keiki ma ka ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi. He moʻolelo ia no kekahi keiki liʻiliʻi a me kona ʻohana.

Ua hāʻawi ʻo Kamalei i ka puke āna i kākau ai i kekahi hui puke ma Honolulu. Makemake ka hui e hoʻopuka i ka puke. Ua paʻi ka hui i 2000 puke. Ua paʻi ʻia nā kiʻi a me nā ʻaoʻao a pau.

I Ianuali, ua hoʻokuʻu ʻia ka puke. Ua hoʻokuʻu ka hui i ka puke ma nā hale kūʻai a ma ka pūnaewele. Ua kūʻai nā kānaka he nui i ka puke a Kamalei. Ma ka hopena o Ianuali, ua loaʻa i ka puke ke kūlana mua ma ka papa helu o nā puke o Hawaiʻi.

He kūlana koʻikoʻi kēia no Kamalei. ʻO kēia ka puke mua āna i kākau ai. I kēia manawa, ke kākau nei ʻo ia i kekahi puke hou. E hoʻopuka ana ka hui i ka puke hou i Iulai.

Nā nīnau:
Ua kākau ʻo Kamalei i ka puke ma ka ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi?
Ua kākau nō ʻo ia i ka puke ma ka ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi.
Ua paʻi ka hui i 2000 puke?
Ua paʻi nō ka hui i 2000 puke.
Ua hoʻokuʻu ʻia ka puke i Ianuali?
Ua hoʻokuʻu ʻia nō ka puke i Ianuali.
He aha ke kūlana o ka puke ma ka papa helu?
Ua loaʻa i ka puke ke kūlana mua.
